title: Nigali Sagar Pillar Edict: The Konakamana stupa
excerpt: Ashoka records enlarging a stupa for the Buddha Konakamana and later visiting the site.
html:
About this edict

This short pillar inscription records two acts at different regnal dates: enlargement of the stupa and the king’s later visit. The facsimile shares a plate with the Lumbini inscription.

Original script

Roman transliteration

The text below follows the Nigali Sagar version in Hultzsch’s edition. Square brackets show restored or uncertain letters; dots mark damaged or missing text. Other surviving copies can differ.

(A) 1 Devānaṃpiyena Piyadasina lājina codasa-vasā[bh]i[si]t[e]n[a] 2 Budhasa Konākamanasa thube dutiyaṃ vaḍhite (B) 3 ........ sābhisitena ca atana āgāca mahīyite 4 .......... pāpite

English translation

This is E. Hultzsch’s 1925 translation of the same version. Its terminology and bracketed restorations reflect that historical edition.

(A) When king Devānāṃpriya Priyadarśin had been anointed fourteen years, he enlarged the Stūpa of the Buddha Konākamana to the double (of its original size). (B) And when he had been anointed [twenty] years, he came himself and worshipped (this spot) [and] caused [a stone pillar to be set up].

Sources

  • E. Hultzsch, Inscriptions of Asoka (1925), Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, volume I.
  • Bibliotheca Polyglotta edition, University of Oslo (Magadhi transliteration, English translation, and inscription facsimiles).
